items.explanation: 80-year-old woman (DOB 1945-10-26) whose cardiology clinic notes of 9/12/2025, 12/31/2025, 3/12/2026 and 5/28/2026 all document persistent atrial fibrillation. CHA2DS2-VASc = 9 (CHF/hypertensive heart disease with heart failure I110+I5040, hypertension I10, age >=75 = 2, type 2 diabetes E119, prior cerebral infarction with residual deficits I69322/I69351 = 2, coronary atherosclerosis I2510, female). Current medications at the last visit (5/28/2026) are aspirin 81 mg and atorvastatin 40 mg only; there is no anticoagulant order active on 2026-09-24. Guideline-recommended oral anticoagulation (Class 1) is absent - needs clinical review.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch list, and above the 20 mg/day maximum advised for QT risk) is the current order (MedicationRequest 7f787d30, 5/29/2026, valid to 12/25/2026); citalopram has been continuous since 10/2/2023. The most recent ECG (104821039, 11/10/2023) shows sinus rhythm at 70/min with QT 508 ms and Bazett QTc 550 ms, above the 500 ms threshold in the QT monitoring memo. Most recent potassium 4.5 mEq/L (1/21/2026) and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (12/1/2023) are normal. No ECG has been obtained since citalopram was continued; prescriber review required.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch list) is the current order (MedicationRequest c6f532e9, 8/22/2026, valid to 1/5/2027); amiodarone has been continuous since 3/1/2022. The most recent ECG (101515306, 4/27/2022) shows sinus rhythm at 58/min with QT 562 ms and Bazett QTc 551 ms, above the 500 ms threshold, and markedly longer than the 4/6/2022 tracing (QTc 433 ms). Most recent electrolytes (2/14/2026) potassium 4.1 mEq/L and magnesium 1.8 mg/dL are within range. The patient also takes warfarin (dose reduced 9/10/2026). Prescriber review required.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 3/2/2026 (MedicationRequest c17946a1). Because the start is on/after 3/1/2026 the revised memo applies: ECG required within 14 days, i.e. by 3/16/2026. ECG 104882441 was recorded 3/7/2026, 5 days after the start - requirement met.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 11/10/2025 (MedicationRequest e578297f). The start falls between 9/1/2025 and 3/1/2026, so the 9/1/2025 memo's 30-day window applies: ECG due by 12/10/2025. ECG 106885519 was recorded 11/24/2025, 14 days after the start - requirement met (that ECG shows QTc 537 ms, raised separately as a QT safety item).

Escitalopram oxalate 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2/12/2026 (MedicationRequest cbe91d0f). The start pre-dates 3/1/2026, so the 30-day window of the 9/1/2025 memo applies (the 3/1/2026 revision explicitly leaves earlier starts on 30 days): ECG due by 3/14/2026. ECG 101538691 was recorded 3/8/2026, 24 days after the start - requirement met.

Escitalopram oxalate 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 4/10/2026 (MedicationRequest 88943096). Start on/after 3/1/2026, so an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 4/24/2026. The only ECG in the chart, 107859369, was recorded 4/29/2026 - 19 days after the start and 5 days past the deadline - so the 14-day requirement was not met and no qualifying ECG exists; the deadline is now long past. (It would have satisfied the superseded 30-day rule.)

Escitalopram oxalate 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 8/1/2026 (MedicationRequest 4dde586a; it first appears on that visit's medication list). Start on/after 3/1/2026, so an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 8/15/2026. The patient's only ECG is 106035722 from 12/25/2025; no ECG has been obtained since the drug was started and the due date has passed.

Escitalopram oxalate 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 8/10/2026 (MedicationRequest f757652a). Start on/after 3/1/2026, so an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 8/24/2026. No ECG for this patient exists in the chart, but the nurse telephone note of 8/25/2026 (DocumentReference 5e12a8aa-0439-53cd-a194-cc1a277d296d) records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 8/18/2026 - within the window - and that the report was requested by fax but not yet received. That outside tracing could satisfy the requirement, so completion cannot be determined until the report arrives.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 9/15/2026 (MedicationRequest 9db19264). Start on/after 3/1/2026, so an ECG is required within 14 days, i.e. by 9/29/2026. No ECG has been recorded since 3/9/2025, but the deadline falls after the 9/24/2026 evaluation date, so the requirement is not yet due.

At the cardiology clinic visit of 9/1/2026 the clinician documented 'INR today 1.6, subtherapeutic. Increase warfarin to 7.5 mg daily; recheck INR' (DocumentReference b32487e8) - a warfarin dose change by a Cardiology Clinic clinician, so the 3/1/2026 memo requires an INR within 7 days, i.e. by 9/8/2026. INR 2.3 was resulted on 9/5/2026 (Observation d6b3bad5), 4 days after the change - requirement met.

48-year-old man (DOB 1978-02-27); every cardiology clinic note from 7/19/2025 through 6/12/2026 documents paroxysmal atrial fibrillation. CHA2DS2-VASc = 2 (congestive heart failure - Condition 1637f513-9a96-5071-9c0b-5013c07d1826 congestive heart failure, 4f51180a-ec61-5073-b4cd-c2c0f1a278d9 acute systolic heart failure, 091ff345-a190-5142-b863-af0c6b7cb15e cardiomyopathy; hypertension - Condition 163efe19-5928-5b4f-80cd-dba90a10d039). A score of 2 in a man carries a Class 1 recommendation for oral anticoagulation, but current medications (last visit 6/12/2026) are famotidine and pantoprazole only and no anticoagulant order is active on 2026-09-24.

The anticoagulation clinic pharmacist note of 9/10/2026 (DocumentReference 9579a764) documents 'Home INR 3.4. Warfarin decreased from 5 mg to 4 mg daily per protocol' - a dose change made by a clinic pharmacist under the standing order, so the 3/1/2026 memo requires an INR within 7 days, i.e. by 9/17/2026. The most recent INR in the chart is 2.6 from 8/22/2026 (before the change); no INR has been resulted since 9/10/2026 and the due date passed 7 days before the 9/24/2026 evaluation.

71-year-old man (DOB 1955-08-23) with coded atrial fibrillation (Condition 7010d0e5, ICD-9 427.31) restated in all cardiology notes through 7/28/2026. CHA2DS2-VASc = 3 (hypertension a85598ce, age 65-74 = 1, coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery 75b86cdb = vascular disease). Current medication is tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily only; no anticoagulant order is active on 2026-09-24. A remote coded 'hemorrhage complicating a procedure' (63df7d4c) is the only bleeding history and is not documented as an active contraindication, so guideline-recommended anticoagulation appears to be missing.

71-year-old woman (DOB 1955-09-07) with coded paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (Condition 66dd1300, ICD-10 I48.0); her single ECG (102298909, 3/14/2025) shows sinus rhythm with an isolated ectopic beat, consistent with paroxysmal AF. CHA2DS2-VASc = 5 (hypertension I10/4019, age 65-74 = 1, prior embolic cerebral infarction I6340/I639 with residual hemiplegia I69354 = 2, female). Current medications (last visit 7/10/2026) are carvedilol 6.25 mg twice daily, metoprolol tartrate 25 mg twice daily and famotidine; no anticoagulant order is active on 2026-09-24, so guideline-recommended (Class 1) oral anticoagulation is absent.

Apixaban 5 mg twice daily was re-ordered at the 8/20/2026 cardiology clinic visit (MedicationRequest dc397aff, valid through 2027) and is the current anticoagulant for atrial flutter. However the 8/12/2026 outside-records summary (DocumentReference 8fcbd349) documents an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer with haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL and 2 units transfused, and states that apixaban was held at discharge pending cardiology review. Anticoagulation has therefore been restarted after a major bleed without the documented review, and the patient is also on aspirin 81 mg plus clopidogrel 75 mg, compounding bleeding risk. Needs prescriber review.

Two different oral anticoagulants are simultaneously active on 2026-09-24: apixaban 5 mg twice daily (MedicationRequest 7206d5b5, authored 7/15/2026, valid to 1/2027) and rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (MedicationRequest b71a461f, authored 7/15/2026, valid to 1/2027). The 7/15/2026 clinic note (DocumentReference a80a007c) states the intent was to switch from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, but the rivaroxaban order was never stopped and the 7/15/2026 medication list still contains both. Duplicate anticoagulation markedly increases bleeding risk in this patient (AF/flutter, CKD stage 3, prior GI/rectal bleeding, thrombocytopenia) and must be reconciled.

The cardiology clinic note of 6/10/2026 (DocumentReference 96cdf346) states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded that same day - 107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36 - show atrial fibrillation: no organised P waves (P-wave amplitude 0.03-0.08 mV with beat-to-beat correlation 0.3-0.7) and markedly irregular RR intervals (coefficient of variation 0.16-0.19) at a mean ventricular rate of 132-136/min. The documented rhythm and rate are contradicted by the same-day tracings.

Escitalopram oxalate 10 mg daily is a QT watch-list drug and is the current order (MedicationRequest 8de890c6, 4/23/2026, valid to 1/2/2027); it has been continuous since it was started on 5/14/2024. The patient's most recent ECG (108018814, 10/8/2023) shows sinus rhythm at 68/min with QT 484 ms and Bazett QTc 516 ms, at or above the 500 ms threshold in the 1/15/2025 QT monitoring memo, so prescriber review is required. Most recent electrolytes (8/23/2025) are potassium 4.1 mEq/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL, both normal, so the prolongation is not explained by electrolyte depletion. Note the clinic note of 5/14/2024 described this tracing as 'QT acceptable'.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch list) is the current order (MedicationRequest 1014aca9, 7/29/2026, valid to 1/5/2027); amiodarone was started at the 11/10/2025 clinic visit. The most recent ECG (106885519, 11/24/2025 - obtained 14 days after amiodarone was started) shows sinus rhythm at 62/min with QT 528 ms and Bazett QTc 537 ms, well above the 500 ms threshold, and is a marked increase from the pre-amiodarone tracing of 6/7/2025 (QTc 423 ms). Most recent electrolytes (4/20/2026) potassium 4.4 mEq/L and magnesium 2.2 mg/dL are normal. The patient is also on warfarin, which amiodarone potentiates. Prescriber review required.

interpretations.explanation: Sinus rhythm at 81/min: upright, uniform P waves (0.22 mV in II, beat-to-beat correlation 0.98) preceding every QRS with regular RR intervals (CV 0.09, normal respiratory variation). PR 186 ms, QRS 78 ms, QT 324 ms, QTc (Bazett, RR 0.74 s) 376 ms. Frontal QRS axis +47 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block and no AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no comparison is possible. Recorded 3/7/2026, concordant with the same-day note 'ECG today: sinus rhythm'.

Sinus tachycardia at 104/min, regular (CV 0.01), with a prominent uniform P wave (0.22 mV, correlation 0.97) before every QRS. PR 144 ms, QRS 96 ms, QT 334 ms, QTc 439 ms. Axis +39 degrees (normal); no bundle branch block or AV block. Compared with the prior ECG 100698634 (6/20/2025: sinus tachycardia 148/min, PR 122 ms, QRS 92 ms, QT 282 ms, QTc about 441 ms) the rate has fallen but rhythm, conduction and QTc are essentially unchanged (QTc change about -2 ms).

Sinus tachycardia at 108/min, regular (CV 0.03), with a uniform P wave before each QRS (correlation 0.98). PR 120 ms, QRS 90 ms, QT 346 ms, QTc (RR 0.55 s) 465 ms - borderline prolonged but below the 500 ms review threshold, and the patient takes no QT watch-list drug. Axis +36 degrees (normal); no bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart (5/21/2024), so no prior comparison.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, mean rate about 136/min: no organised P activity (pre-QRS deflection 0.08-0.11 mV with beat-to-beat correlation only 0.3-0.5) and irregularly irregular RR intervals (CV 0.16). No measurable PR interval. QRS 96 ms, QT 284 ms, QTc (mean RR 0.44 s) 428 ms. Axis -2 degrees (normal); no bundle branch block. The prior tracing 107914094 was taken 2 hours 23 minutes earlier the same day (6/10/2026) and also shows atrial fibrillation at 132/min with QRS 98 ms and QTc 431 ms, so there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc. Note that the clinic note of 6/10/2026 describes these tracings as 'normal sinus rhythm, rate 72', which the ECGs contradict (raised as a separate review item).

Sinus rhythm at 69/min, regular (CV 0.005), with a low-amplitude but consistent P wave before each QRS (correlation 0.91). PR 160 ms, QRS 78 ms, QT 394 ms, QTc 421 ms. Axis -25 degrees (normal, within -30 to +90). No bundle branch block or AV block. Versus prior ECG 104232242 (4/27/2025: sinus 61/min, PR 124 ms, QRS 78 ms, QTc 404 ms, with an extreme/right-superior axis of about -174 degrees) the rhythm, QRS duration and QTc (+17 ms) are unchanged; the frontal axis differs but axis shift is not a reportable change category.

Sinus rhythm at 98/min, regular (CV 0.02), with a uniform P wave (0.18 mV, correlation 0.93) before every QRS. PR 116 ms, QRS 76 ms, QT 310 ms, QTc 395 ms. Axis +6 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block, no AV block. Only ECG in the chart (5/23/2024), so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 72/min, regular (CV 0.01), with a consistent P wave before each QRS (correlation 0.94). PR 144 ms, QRS 82 ms, QT 368 ms, QTc 404 ms - normal. Axis +21 degrees (normal); no bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart (12/25/2025), so no prior comparison. This tracing pre-dates the escitalopram start of 8/1/2026, so it does not satisfy the post-start ECG requirement (raised separately).

Atrial fibrillation at a mean ventricular rate of about 61/min: no organised P waves (0.04 mV residual, beat-to-beat correlation 0.46) and irregularly irregular RR intervals (CV 0.20). No measurable PR interval. QRS 90 ms, QT 438 ms, QTc (mean RR 0.98 s) 443 ms. Axis +28 degrees (normal); no bundle branch block. The prior ECG 107873952 (11/12/2024, three days earlier) showed sinus rhythm at 69/min with a well formed P wave (0.24 mV, correlation 0.97), PR 174 ms, QRS 82 ms and QTc 402 ms, so atrial fibrillation is new on this tracing; the QTc change (+41 ms) is under 60 ms.

Sinus bradycardia at 58/min, regular (CV 0.03), with a uniform P wave before every QRS (correlation 1.00). PR 112 ms, QRS 86 ms, QT 420 ms, QTc 414 ms. Axis +60 degrees (normal); no bundle branch block or AV block. Versus prior ECG 106045460 (3/8/2025, the previous day: sinus 62/min, PR 110 ms, QRS 88 ms, QTc 444 ms) rhythm and conduction are unchanged and the QTc change (-30 ms) is under 60 ms. Note haloperidol was only started 9/15/2026, after both tracings.

Sinus rhythm at 83/min, essentially perfectly regular (CV 0.004), with a uniform P wave before each QRS (correlation 0.99). PR 150 ms, QRS 72 ms, QT 348 ms, QTc 410 ms. Axis +52 degrees (normal); no bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart (8/23/2025), so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 76/min, regular (CV 0.01), with a prominent uniform P wave (0.26 mV, correlation 0.98) before every QRS. PR 156 ms, QRS 70 ms, QT 392 ms, QTc 442 ms. Axis +64 degrees (normal); no bundle branch block or AV block. The prior ECG 109048192 (2/2/2020: sinus 75/min, PR 140 ms, QRS 82 ms, QT 466 ms, QTc 515 ms with a flat, late, low-amplitude T wave) had a distinctly longer repolarisation; the QTc has fallen by about 73 ms, i.e. by 60 ms or more. Rhythm and conduction are otherwise unchanged.

Sinus tachycardia at 121/min with a uniform P wave before each QRS (0.20 mV, correlation 0.99) and near-perfectly regular RR intervals (CV 0.005). PR 190 ms, QRS 94 ms, QT 278 ms, QTc 394 ms. Axis +53 degrees (normal). No conduction block. Compared with the prior tracing 106186980 (9/16/2016, sinus at 108/min, PR 172 ms, QRS 94 ms, QTc 402 ms, axis +46): unchanged rhythm, no new conduction abnormality and QTc change only -8 ms, so no reportable changes.

Sinus rhythm at 55/min (sinus bradycardia), regular (CV 0.01), with a uniform P wave before every QRS (correlation 0.98). The PR interval is prolonged at about 220 ms (P onset -128 ms, QRS onset -19 ms relative to the R peak), i.e. first-degree AV block; every P is followed by a QRS so there is no higher-grade block. QRS 84 ms (no bundle branch block), QT 400 ms, QTc (RR 1.10 s) 381 ms. Axis about 0 degrees (normal). Versus prior ECG 103042067 (11/30/2024: sinus 51/min, PR about 190 ms, QRS 86 ms, QTc 365 ms) the rhythm is unchanged and the QTc change (+16 ms) is well under 60 ms; the first-degree AV block is not a listed change category.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, mean rate about 151/min: no organised atrial activity phase-locked to the QRS (pre-QRS deflection correlation only 0.01-0.23 across beats) and markedly irregular RR intervals ranging 288-580 ms (CV 0.19). No measurable PR interval. QRS 98 ms, QT 268 ms, QTc (mean RR 0.40 s) 426 ms. Axis -20 degrees (normal); no bundle branch block. The prior ECG 107374881 (9/12/2025, the previous day) showed sinus rhythm at 77/min with a discrete P wave (correlation 0.88), PR 146 ms, QRS 94 ms and QTc 422 ms, so atrial fibrillation is new; QTc essentially unchanged (+4 ms).

Sinus rhythm at 72/min, regular (CV 0.05), with a prominent uniform P wave (0.22 mV, correlation 0.99) before every QRS. PR 170 ms, QRS 92 ms, QT 360 ms, QTc 394 ms - normal. Axis +12 degrees (normal); no bundle branch block or AV block. The prior ECG 105362569 (11/21/2025, two days earlier: sinus 67/min, PR 152 ms, QRS 90 ms, QT 506 ms, QTc 535 ms) showed marked QT prolongation which has resolved: the QTc has fallen by about 141 ms, i.e. by 60 ms or more. Concordant with the 11/23/2025 note 'ECG today: sinus rhythm'.

Sinus rhythm at 74/min, regular (CV 0.02), with a uniform P wave before each QRS (correlation 0.88). PR about 192 ms - at the upper limit of normal but below 200 ms, so not first-degree AV block. QRS 88 ms, QT 378 ms, QTc 419 ms. Axis +59 degrees (normal); no bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart (2/15/2025), so no prior comparison.

Sinus tachycardia at 112/min, essentially perfectly regular (CV 0.002), with a single uniform P wave (0.19 mV, correlation 0.96) before every QRS and a clearly isoelectric PR segment - no flutter waves and no 2:1 atrial activity despite the coded history of atrial flutter. PR 160 ms, QRS 94 ms, QT 290 ms, QTc 395 ms. Axis +35 degrees (normal); no bundle branch block or AV block. Versus prior ECG 102955795 (7/4/2022: sinus 115/min, PR 162 ms, QRS 92 ms, QTc 393 ms) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc (+3 ms).

Sinus rhythm at a mean rate of about 62/min with a uniform P wave before each conducted QRS. The RR intervals are regular at about 980 ms apart from one early beat (RR 544 ms) followed by a compensatory pause (1364 ms) - an isolated ectopic beat, which accounts for the overall RR variability; this is not atrial fibrillation. The PR interval is prolonged at about 204 ms (P onset -127 ms, QRS onset -25 ms relative to R), i.e. first-degree AV block. QRS 98 ms (no bundle branch block), QT 402 ms, QTc 408 ms. Frontal axis about -31 degrees - left axis deviation (net QRS negative in leads II and aVF). Only ECG in the chart (3/14/2025), so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 70/min, regular (CV 0.02), with a consistent P wave before each QRS (correlation 0.84). PR 146 ms, QRS 92 ms, QT 360 ms, QTc 388 ms - normal. Frontal QRS axis about -173 degrees: the QRS is deeply negative in I and aVL and only slightly negative in aVF, giving an extreme (right-superior) axis. No bundle branch block and no AV block. Only ECG in the chart (4/29/2026), so no prior comparison; note this tracing was obtained 19 days after escitalopram was started, outside the required 14-day window (raised separately).

Sinus rhythm at 70/min, regular (CV 0.03), with a consistent P wave before each QRS (correlation 0.94). PR 160 ms, QRS 100 ms, QT 508 ms, QTc (Bazett, RR 0.85 s) 550 ms - markedly prolonged with a broad, flat T wave. Axis +37 degrees (normal); QRS duration below 120 ms so no bundle branch block, and no AV block. Versus prior ECG 107149156 (6/17/2020: sinus tachycardia 132/min, PR 144 ms, QRS 90 ms, QTc about 448 ms) the QTc has increased by roughly 100 ms, i.e. by 60 ms or more. The patient takes citalopram 40 mg daily; raised separately as a QT safety item.

Sinus rhythm at 68/min, regular (CV 0.03), with a P wave before each QRS. PR about 158 ms, QRS 82 ms, QT 390 ms, QTc 416 ms. Frontal axis about +85 degrees - vertical but still within the normal range (-30 to +90). No bundle branch block and no AV block. Only ECG in the chart (3/8/2026); it was obtained 24 days after escitalopram was started on 2/12/2026 and satisfies the then-applicable 30-day monitoring rule.

Sinus bradycardia at 53/min, regular (CV 0.02), with a uniform P wave (0.18 mV, correlation 0.94) before every QRS. PR 188 ms (upper normal, below 200 ms), QRS 92 ms, QT 396 ms, QTc (RR 1.14 s) 372 ms. Axis -5 degrees (normal); no bundle branch block or AV block. Versus prior ECG 108651109 (12/13/2018: sinus 66/min, PR about 200 ms, QRS 100 ms, QTc 389 ms) rhythm and conduction are unchanged and the QTc change (-17 ms) is under 60 ms.

Sinus rhythm at 68/min, regular (CV 0.01) with a consistent P wave before each QRS. PR 130 ms, QRS 88 ms, QT 484 ms, QTc (Bazett, RR 0.88 s) 516 ms - markedly prolonged. Axis +44 degrees (normal); no bundle branch block or AV block. Versus the prior ECG 100065910 (11/23/2022: sinus 75/min, PR 118 ms, QRS 88 ms, QTc 357 ms) the QTc has increased by about 159 ms, well beyond 60 ms. The interval prolongation follows the start of escitalopram on 5/14/2024 and is raised separately as a QT safety item.

Sinus tachycardia at 141/min: a small but uniform P wave precedes every QRS (beat-to-beat correlation 0.98) and the RR intervals are regular (404-454 ms, CV 0.02); there is a single atrial wave per cycle, so this is not 2:1 atrial flutter. PR 138 ms, QRS 84 ms, QT 274 ms, QTc (mean RR 0.43 s) 420 ms. Axis +2 degrees (normal); no bundle branch block or AV block. The prior ECG 109839112 (7/11/2022) showed atrial fibrillation - absent organised P waves (0.02-0.03 mV, correlation 0.5-0.7) with grossly irregular RR intervals (CV 0.24) at 105/min - so atrial fibrillation has resolved (sinus rhythm restored). QTc essentially unchanged (-3 ms).

Sinus rhythm at 82/min, regular (CV 0.01), with a uniform P wave before each QRS (correlation 0.99). PR about 175 ms, QRS 102 ms - slightly wide but below 120 ms, so no bundle branch block. QT 382 ms, QTc 448 ms. Axis +34 degrees (normal); no AV block. Only ECG in the chart (5/12/2025), so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 91/min, regular (CV 0.01), with a uniform P wave before every QRS (correlation 1.00). PR about 170 ms, QRS 80 ms, QT 334 ms, QTc 412 ms. Axis -18 degrees (normal); no bundle branch block and no AV block. Versus prior ECG 102616671 (5/16/2021: sinus 87/min, PR about 142 ms, QRS 82 ms, QTc 396 ms) rhythm, conduction and QTc (+16 ms) are unchanged.

Sinus rhythm at 59/min with a P wave before every QRS (correlation 0.92) and regular RR intervals (CV 0.08). PR 186 ms. The QRS is broad at 130 ms with a deep, broad negative complex in V1-V2 (net area -62 mV.ms, nadir -1.4 mV) and a broad monophasic R wave in I, aVL and V5-V6 (V6 R 1.34 mV, net area +44 mV.ms) without a septal q - complete left bundle branch block. QT 440 ms, QTc 436 ms. Frontal axis -21 degrees (normal). Versus prior ECG 103686933 (6/3/2024: sinus 68/min, PR 192 ms, QRS also 130 ms with the same left bundle branch block morphology, QTc 453 ms) there is no change in rhythm, the bundle branch block is unchanged (not new), and the QTc change (-17 ms) is under 60 ms.

Sinus rhythm at 102/min, regular (CV 0.01), with a uniform P wave before each QRS (correlation 0.99). PR about 180 ms, QRS 88 ms, QT 332 ms, QTc 433 ms. Axis +44 degrees (normal); no bundle branch block or AV block. Versus prior ECG 101016166 (3/18/2025, the previous day: sinus 101/min, PR about 170 ms, QRS 86 ms, QTc 437 ms) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc (-4 ms).

Sinus rhythm at 66/min, regular (CV 0.02), with a consistent P wave before each QRS (correlation 0.89). PR about 176 ms, QRS 88 ms, QT 374 ms, QTc 391 ms - all normal. Axis -20 degrees (normal); no bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart (9/22/2025), so no prior comparison.

Sinus bradycardia at 58/min with a uniform P wave before every QRS (correlation 0.84) and regular RR intervals (CV 0.05). The PR interval is prolonged at about 208 ms (P onset -127 ms, QRS onset -23 ms relative to R), i.e. first-degree AV block. QRS 88 ms (no bundle branch block), QT 562 ms, QTc (Bazett, RR 1.04 s) 551 ms - markedly prolonged. Axis +37 degrees (normal). The prior ECG 100867733 (4/6/2022) showed atrial fibrillation - no organised P waves (0.02-0.03 mV, correlation 0.53) with irregularly irregular RR intervals (CV 0.19) at 130/min, QTc about 433-444 ms - so atrial fibrillation has resolved and the QTc has increased by roughly 110-120 ms, i.e. by 60 ms or more. The patient is on amiodarone; raised separately as a QT safety item.

Sinus tachycardia at 107/min, regular (CV 0.01), with a prominent uniform P wave (0.22 mV, correlation 0.90) before every QRS. PR 162 ms, QRS 72 ms, QT 332 ms, QTc 444 ms. Axis +54 degrees (normal); no bundle branch block or AV block. Versus prior ECG 107274479 (7/27/2019: sinus 75/min, PR about 150 ms, QRS 72 ms, QTc 437 ms) rhythm, conduction and QTc (+7 ms) are unchanged.

Sinus tachycardia at 121/min, regular (CV 0.005), with a discrete P wave (0.11 mV) before every QRS. PR 132 ms, QRS 84 ms, QT 290 ms, QTc 412 ms. Axis +68 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block, no AV block. Single ECG in the chart (4/19/2024), so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 102/min, regular (CV 0.02), uniform P waves (0.17 mV, correlation 0.99). PR 158 ms, QRS 88 ms, QT 316 ms, QTc 411 ms. Axis +58 degrees (normal); no conduction abnormality. The prior tracing 102910502 was recorded one minute earlier the same day (8/23/2021) and is essentially identical (sinus 100/min, PR 148 ms, QRS 88 ms, QTc 408 ms, axis +61): no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc (+3 ms).

Sinus bradycardia at 52/min, regular (CV 0.01), with a low-amplitude but consistent P wave before each QRS (correlation 0.98). PR 182 ms, QRS 90 ms, QT 416 ms, QTc (RR 1.16 s) 386 ms. Axis +36 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block; PR below 200 ms so no first-degree AV block. Versus prior ECG 104629882 (5/22/2023: sinus 58/min, PR 142 ms, QRS 88 ms, QTc 353 ms, axis +16) there is no rhythm change, no new conduction block and the QTc change (+33 ms) is under 60 ms.

Sinus tachycardia at 122/min, essentially perfectly regular (CV 0.002), with a uniform P wave before each QRS (correlation 0.99). PR 128 ms, QRS 94 ms (normal duration), QT 292 ms, QTc 416 ms. Frontal QRS axis about +139 degrees - right axis deviation. No bundle branch block and no AV block on this tracing. The prior ECG 106516875, recorded 13 hours earlier the same day (12/5/2024 01:33), showed the same sinus mechanism but a QRS of 154 ms with an rSR' pattern in V1-V2 (terminal R 1.1 mV) and a broad terminal S in I, aVL and V5-V6 - complete right bundle branch block - together with a QTc of 481 ms. The right bundle branch block has resolved on the 14:38 tracing and the QTc has fallen by about 65 ms (481 to 416 ms), i.e. by 60 ms or more.

Sinus rhythm at 62/min, regular (CV 0.01), with a consistent P wave before each QRS. PR 138 ms, QRS 98 ms, QT 528 ms, QTc (Bazett, RR 0.97 s) 537 ms - markedly prolonged with a broad, late T wave. Axis +66 degrees (normal); no bundle branch block or AV block. Versus prior ECG 108780865 (6/7/2025: sinus bradycardia 49/min, PR 186 ms, QRS 98 ms, QTc 425 ms) the QTc has risen by about 112 ms, far beyond 60 ms. Amiodarone was started 11/10/2025, 14 days before this tracing; raised separately as a QT safety item.

Atrial fibrillation with a mean ventricular rate of about 101/min: no organised P waves (residual pre-QRS deflection only 0.036 mV with beat-to-beat correlation 0.54) and grossly irregular RR intervals (coefficient of variation 0.29). No measurable PR interval. QRS 80 ms, QT 328 ms, QTc (mean RR 0.60 s) 425 ms. Frontal axis -53 degrees - left axis deviation. No bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart (9/17/2024), so no prior comparison. The patient is on warfarin.

arguments.explanation: Sinus rhythm at a mean rate of about 62/min with a uniform P wave before each conducted QRS. The RR intervals are regular at about 980 ms apart from one early beat (RR 544 ms) followed by a compensatory pause (1364 ms) - an isolated ectopic beat, which accounts for the overall RR variability; this is not atrial fibrillation. The PR interval is prolonged at about 204 ms (P onset -127 ms, QRS onset -25 ms relative to R), i.e. first-degree AV block. QRS 98 ms (no bundle branch block), QT 402 ms, QTc 408 ms. Frontal axis about -31 degrees - left axis deviation (net QRS negative in leads II and aVF). Only ECG in the chart (3/14/2025), so no prior comparison.

Recorded 3/7/2026, concordant with the same-day note 'ECG today: sinus rhythm'.

Sinus tachycardia at 104/min, regular (CV 0.01), with a prominent uniform P wave (0.22 mV, correlation 0.97) before every QRS. PR 144 ms, QRS 96 ms, QT 334 ms, QTc 439 ms. Axis +39 degrees (normal); no bundle branch block or AV block. Compared with the prior ECG 100698634 (6/20/2025: sinus tachycardia 148/min, PR 122 ms, QRS 92 ms, QT 282 ms, QTc about 441 ms) the rate has fallen but rhythm, conduction and QTc are essentially unchanged (QTc change about -2 ms).

Sinus tachycardia at 108/min, regular (CV 0.03), with a uniform P wave before each QRS (correlation 0.98). PR 120 ms, QRS 90 ms, QT 346 ms, QTc (RR 0.55 s) 465 ms - borderline prolonged but below the 500 ms review threshold, and the patient takes no QT watch-list drug. Axis +36 degrees (normal); no bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart (5/21/2024), so no prior comparison.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, mean rate about 136/min: no organised P activity (pre-QRS deflection 0.08-0.11 mV with beat-to-beat correlation only 0.3-0.5) and irregularly irregular RR intervals (CV 0.16). No measurable PR interval. QRS 96 ms, QT 284 ms, QTc (mean RR 0.44 s) 428 ms. Axis -2 degrees (normal); no bundle branch block. The prior tracing 107914094 was taken 2 hours 23 minutes earlier the same day (6/10/2026) and also shows atrial fibrillation at 132/min with QRS 98 ms and QTc 431 ms, so there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc. Note that the clinic note of 6/10/2026 describes these tracings as 'normal sinus rhythm, rate 72', which the ECGs contradict (raised as a separate review item).

Sinus rhythm at 69/min, regular (CV 0.005), with a low-amplitude but consistent P wave before each QRS (correlation 0.91). PR 160 ms, QRS 78 ms, QT 394 ms, QTc 421 ms. Axis -25 degrees (normal, within -30 to +90). No bundle branch block or AV block. Versus prior ECG 104232242 (4/27/2025: sinus 61/min, PR 124 ms, QRS 78 ms, QTc 404 ms, with an extreme/right-superior axis of about -174 degrees) the rhythm, QRS duration and QTc (+17 ms) are unchanged; the frontal axis differs but axis shift is not a reportable change category.

Sinus rhythm at 98/min, regular (CV 0.02), with a uniform P wave (0.18 mV, correlation 0.93) before every QRS. PR 116 ms, QRS 76 ms, QT 310 ms, QTc 395 ms. Axis +6 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block, no AV block. Only ECG in the chart (5/23/2024), so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 72/min, regular (CV 0.01), with a consistent P wave before each QRS (correlation 0.94). PR 144 ms, QRS 82 ms, QT 368 ms, QTc 404 ms - normal. Axis +21 degrees (normal); no bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart (12/25/2025), so no prior comparison. This tracing pre-dates the escitalopram start of 8/1/2026, so it does not satisfy the post-start ECG requirement (raised separately).

Atrial fibrillation at a mean ventricular rate of about 61/min: no organised P waves (0.04 mV residual, beat-to-beat correlation 0.46) and irregularly irregular RR intervals (CV 0.20). Sinus bradycardia at 58/min, regular (CV 0.03), with a uniform P wave before every QRS (correlation 1.00). PR 112 ms, QRS 86 ms, QT 420 ms, QTc 414 ms. Axis +60 degrees (normal); no bundle branch block or AV block. Versus prior ECG 106045460 (3/8/2025, the previous day: sinus 62/min, PR 110 ms, QRS 88 ms, QTc 444 ms) rhythm and conduction are unchanged and the QTc change (-30 ms) is under 60 ms. Note haloperidol was only started 9/15/2026, after both tracings.

Sinus rhythm at 83/min, essentially perfectly regular (CV 0.004), with a uniform P wave before each QRS (correlation 0.99). PR 150 ms, QRS 72 ms, QT 348 ms, QTc 410 ms. Axis +52 degrees (normal); no bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart (8/23/2025), so no prior comparison.

The prior ECG 109048192 (2/2/2020: sinus 75/min, PR 140 ms, QRS 82 ms, QT 466 ms, QTc 515 ms with a flat, late, low-amplitude T wave) had a distinctly longer repolarisation; the QTc has fallen by about 73 ms, i.e. by 60 ms or more. Sinus tachycardia at 121/min with a uniform P wave before each QRS (0.20 mV, correlation 0.99) and near-perfectly regular RR intervals (CV 0.005). PR 190 ms, QRS 94 ms, QT 278 ms, QTc 394 ms. Sinus rhythm at 55/min (sinus bradycardia), regular (CV 0.01), with a uniform P wave before every QRS (correlation 0.98). The PR interval is prolonged at about 220 ms (P onset -128 ms, QRS onset -19 ms relative to the R peak), i.e. first-degree AV block; every P is followed by a QRS so there is no higher-grade block. QRS 84 ms (no bundle branch block), QT 400 ms, QTc (RR 1.10 s) 381 ms. Axis about 0 degrees (normal). Versus prior ECG 103042067 (11/30/2024: sinus 51/min, PR about 190 ms, QRS 86 ms, QTc 365 ms) the rhythm is unchanged and the QTc change (+16 ms) is well under 60 ms; the first-degree AV block is not a listed change category.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, mean rate about 151/min: no organised atrial activity phase-locked to the QRS (pre-QRS deflection correlation only 0.01-0.23 across beats) and markedly irregular RR intervals ranging 288-580 ms (CV 0.19). No measurable PR interval. QRS 98 ms, QT 268 ms, QTc (mean RR 0.40 s) 426 ms. Axis -20 degrees (normal); no bundle branch block. The prior ECG 107374881 (9/12/2025, the previous day) showed sinus rhythm at 77/min with a discrete P wave (correlation 0.88), PR 146 ms, QRS 94 ms and QTc 422 ms, so atrial fibrillation is new; QTc essentially unchanged (+4 ms).

Sinus rhythm at 72/min, regular (CV 0.05), with a prominent uniform P wave (0.22 mV, correlation 0.99) before every QRS. PR 170 ms, QRS 92 ms, QT 360 ms, QTc 394 ms - normal. Axis +12 degrees (normal); no bundle branch block or AV block. The prior ECG 105362569 (11/21/2025, two days earlier: sinus 67/min, PR 152 ms, QRS 90 ms, QT 506 ms, QTc 535 ms) showed marked QT prolongation which has resolved: the QTc has fallen by about 141 ms, i.e. by 60 ms or more. Concordant with the 11/23/2025 note 'ECG today: sinus rhythm'.

Sinus rhythm at 74/min, regular (CV 0.02), with a uniform P wave before each QRS (correlation 0.88). PR about 192 ms - at the upper limit of normal but below 200 ms, so not first-degree AV block. QRS 88 ms, QT 378 ms, QTc 419 ms. Axis +59 degrees (normal); no bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart (2/15/2025), so no prior comparison.

Sinus tachycardia at 112/min, essentially perfectly regular (CV 0.002), with a single uniform P wave (0.19 mV, correlation 0.96) before every QRS and a clearly isoelectric PR segment - no flutter waves and no 2:1 atrial activity despite the coded history of atrial flutter. PR 160 ms, QRS 94 ms, QT 290 ms, QTc 395 ms. Axis +35 degrees (normal); no bundle branch block or AV block. Versus prior ECG 102955795 (7/4/2022: sinus 115/min, PR 162 ms, QRS 92 ms, QTc 393 ms) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc (+3 ms).

Sinus rhythm at a mean rate of about 62/min with a uniform P wave before each conducted QRS. The RR intervals are regular at about 980 ms apart from one early beat (RR 544 ms) followed by a compensatory pause (1364 ms) - an isolated ectopic beat, which accounts for the overall RR variability; this is not atrial fibrillation. The PR interval is prolonged at about 204 ms (P onset -127 ms, QRS onset -25 ms relative to R), i.e. first-degree AV block. QRS 98 ms (no bundle branch block), QT 402 ms, QTc 408 ms. Frontal axis about -31 degrees - left axis deviation (net QRS negative in leads II and aVF). Only ECG in the chart (3/14/2025), so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 70/min, regular (CV 0.02), with a consistent P wave before each QRS (correlation 0.84). PR 146 ms, QRS 92 ms, QT 360 ms, QTc 388 ms - normal. Frontal QRS axis about -173 degrees: the QRS is deeply negative in I and aVL and only slightly negative in aVF, giving an extreme (right-superior) axis. No bundle branch block and no AV block. Only ECG in the chart (4/29/2026), so no prior comparison; note this tracing was obtained 19 days after escitalopram was started, outside the required 14-day window (raised separately).

Sinus rhythm at 70/min, regular (CV 0.03), with a consistent P wave before each QRS (correlation 0.94). PR 160 ms, QRS 100 ms, QT 508 ms, QTc (Bazett, RR 0.85 s) 550 ms - markedly prolonged with a broad, flat T wave. Axis +37 degrees (normal); QRS duration below 120 ms so no bundle branch block, and no AV block. Versus prior ECG 107149156 (6/17/2020: sinus tachycardia 132/min, PR 144 ms, QRS 90 ms, QTc about 448 ms) the QTc has increased by roughly 100 ms, i.e. by 60 ms or more. The patient takes citalopram 40 mg daily; raised separately as a QT safety item.

Sinus rhythm at 68/min, regular (CV 0.03), with a P wave before each QRS. PR about 158 ms, QRS 82 ms, QT 390 ms, QTc 416 ms. Frontal axis about +85 degrees - vertical but still within the normal range (-30 to +90). No bundle branch block and no AV block. Only ECG in the chart (3/8/2026); it was obtained 24 days after escitalopram was started on 2/12/2026 and satisfies the then-applicable 30-day monitoring rule.

Sinus bradycardia at 53/min, regular (CV 0.02), with a uniform P wave (0.18 mV, correlation 0.94) before every QRS. PR 188 ms (upper normal, below 200 ms), QRS 92 ms, QT 396 ms, QTc (RR 1.14 s) 372 ms. Axis -5 degrees (normal); no bundle branch block or AV block. Versus prior ECG 108651109 (12/13/2018: sinus 66/min, PR about 200 ms, QRS 100 ms, QTc 389 ms) rhythm and conduction are unchanged and the QTc change (-17 ms) is under 60 ms.

Sinus rhythm at 68/min, regular (CV 0.01) with a consistent P wave before each QRS. PR 130 ms, QRS 88 ms, QT 484 ms, QTc (Bazett, RR 0.88 s) 516 ms - markedly prolonged. Axis +44 degrees (normal); no bundle branch block or AV block. Versus the prior ECG 100065910 (11/23/2022: sinus 75/min, PR 118 ms, QRS 88 ms, QTc 357 ms) the QTc has increased by about 159 ms, well beyond 60 ms. The interval prolongation follows the start of escitalopram on 5/14/2024 and is raised separately as a QT safety item.

PR 138 ms, QRS 84 ms, QT 274 ms, QTc (mean RR 0.43 s) 420 ms. Axis +2 degrees (normal); no bundle branch block or AV block. The prior ECG 109839112 (7/11/2022) showed atrial fibrillation - absent organised P waves (0.02-0.03 mV, correlation 0.5-0.7) with grossly irregular RR intervals (CV 0.24) at 105/min - so atrial fibrillation has resolved (sinus rhythm restored). Sinus tachycardia at 121/min, regular (CV 0.005), with a discrete P wave (0.11 mV) before every QRS. PR 132 ms, QRS 84 ms, QT 290 ms, QTc 412 ms. Axis +68 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block, no AV block. Single ECG in the chart (4/19/2024), so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 102/min, regular (CV 0.02), uniform P waves (0.17 mV, correlation 0.99). PR 158 ms, QRS 88 ms, QT 316 ms, QTc 411 ms. Axis +58 degrees (normal); no conduction abnormality. The prior tracing 102910502 was recorded one minute earlier the same day (8/23/2021) and is essentially identical (sinus 100/min, PR 148 ms, QRS 88 ms, QTc 408 ms, axis +61): no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc (+3 ms).

Sinus bradycardia at 52/min, regular (CV 0.01), with a low-amplitude but consistent P wave before each QRS (correlation 0.98). PR 182 ms, QRS 90 ms, QT 416 ms, QTc (RR 1.16 s) 386 ms. Versus prior ECG 104629882 (5/22/2023: sinus 58/min, PR 142 ms, QRS 88 ms, QTc 353 ms, axis +16) there is no rhythm change, no new conduction block and the QTc change (+33 ms) is under 60 ms.

Sinus tachycardia at 122/min, essentially perfectly regular (CV 0.002), with a uniform P wave before each QRS (correlation 0.99). PR 128 ms, QRS 94 ms (normal duration), QT 292 ms, QTc 416 ms. Frontal QRS axis about +139 degrees - right axis deviation. No bundle branch block and no AV block on this tracing. The right bundle branch block has resolved on the 14:38 tracing and the QTc has fallen by about 65 ms (481 to 416 ms), i.e. by 60 ms or more.

Sinus rhythm at 62/min, regular (CV 0.01), with a consistent P wave before each QRS. PR 138 ms, QRS 98 ms, QT 528 ms, QTc (Bazett, RR 0.97 s) 537 ms - markedly prolonged with a broad, late T wave. Axis +66 degrees (normal); no bundle branch block or AV block. Versus prior ECG 108780865 (6/7/2025: sinus bradycardia 49/min, PR 186 ms, QRS 98 ms, QTc 425 ms) the QTc has risen by about 112 ms, far beyond 60 ms. Amiodarone was started 11/10/2025, 14 days before this tracing; raised separately as a QT safety item.

Atrial fibrillation with a mean ventricular rate of about 101/min: no organised P waves (residual pre-QRS deflection only 0.036 mV with beat-to-beat correlation 0.54) and grossly irregular RR intervals (coefficient of variation 0.29). No measurable PR interval. QRS 80 ms, QT 328 ms, QTc (mean RR 0.60 s) 425 ms. Frontal axis -53 degrees - left axis deviation. No bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart (9/17/2024), so no prior comparison. The patient is on warfarin.

items.explanation: 80-year-old woman (DOB 1945-10-26) whose cardiology clinic notes of 9/12/2025, 12/31/2025, 3/12/2026 and 5/28/2026 all document persistent atrial fibrillation. CHA2DS2-VASc = 9 (CHF/hypertensive heart disease with heart failure I110+I5040, hypertension I10, age >=75 = 2, type 2 diabetes E119, prior cerebral infarction with residual deficits I69322/I69351 = 2, coronary atherosclerosis I2510, female). Current medications at the last visit (5/28/2026) are aspirin 81 mg and atorvastatin 40 mg only; there is no anticoagulant order active on 2026-09-24. Guideline-recommended oral anticoagulation (Class 1) is absent - needs clinical review.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch list, and above the 20 mg/day maximum advised for QT risk) is the current order (MedicationRequest 7f787d30, 5/29/2026, valid to 12/25/2026); citalopram has been continuous since 10/2/2023. The most recent ECG (104821039, 11/10/2023) shows sinus rhythm at 70/min with QT 508 ms and Bazett QTc 550 ms, above the 500 ms threshold in the QT monitoring memo. Most recent potassium 4.5 mEq/L (1/21/2026) and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (12/1/2023) are normal. No ECG has been obtained since citalopram was continued; prescriber review required.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch list) is the current order (MedicationRequest c6f532e9, 8/22/2026, valid to 1/5/2027); amiodarone has been continuous since 3/1/2022. The most recent ECG (101515306, 4/27/2022) shows sinus rhythm at 58/min with QT 562 ms and Bazett QTc 551 ms, above the 500 ms threshold, and markedly longer than the 4/6/2022 tracing (QTc 433 ms). Most recent electrolytes (2/14/2026) potassium 4.1 mEq/L and magnesium 1.8 mg/dL are within range. The patient also takes warfarin (dose reduced 9/10/2026). Prescriber review required.

Because the start is on/after 3/1/2026 the revised memo applies: ECG required within 14 days, i.e. by 3/16/2026. ECG 104882441 was recorded 3/7/2026, 5 days after the start - requirement met.

ECG 106885519 was recorded 11/24/2025, 14 days after the start - requirement met (that ECG shows QTc 537 ms, raised separately as a QT safety item).

The start pre-dates 3/1/2026, so the 30-day window of the 9/1/2025 memo applies (the 3/1/2026 revision explicitly leaves earlier starts on 30 days): ECG due by 3/14/2026. ECG 101538691 was recorded 3/8/2026, 24 days after the start - requirement met.

The patient's only ECG is 106035722 from 12/25/2025; no ECG has been obtained since the drug was started and the due date has passed.

Start on/after 3/1/2026, so an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 8/24/2026. That outside tracing could satisfy the requirement, so completion cannot be determined until the report arrives.

Start on/after 3/1/2026, so an ECG is required within 14 days, i.e. by 9/29/2026. No ECG has been recorded since 3/9/2025, but the deadline falls after the 9/24/2026 evaluation date, so the requirement is not yet due.

Increase warfarin to 7.5 mg daily; recheck INR' (DocumentReference b32487e8) - a warfarin dose change by a Cardiology Clinic clinician, so the 3/1/2026 memo requires an INR within 7 days, i.e. by 9/8/2026. INR 2.3 was resulted on 9/5/2026 (Observation d6b3bad5), 4 days after the change - requirement met.

CHA2DS2-VASc = 2 (congestive heart failure - Condition 1637f513-9a96-5071-9c0b-5013c07d1826 congestive heart failure, 4f51180a-ec61-5073-b4cd-c2c0f1a278d9 acute systolic heart failure, 091ff345-a190-5142-b863-af0c6b7cb15e cardiomyopathy; hypertension - Condition 163efe19-5928-5b4f-80cd-dba90a10d039). A score of 2 in a man carries a Class 1 recommendation for oral anticoagulation, but current medications (last visit 6/12/2026) are famotidine and pantoprazole only and no anticoagulant order is active on 2026-09-24.

The anticoagulation clinic pharmacist note of 9/10/2026 (DocumentReference 9579a764) documents 'Home INR 3.4. Warfarin decreased from 5 mg to 4 mg daily per protocol' - a dose change made by a clinic pharmacist under the standing order, so the 3/1/2026 memo requires an INR within 7 days, i.e. by 9/17/2026. The most recent INR in the chart is 2.6 from 8/22/2026 (before the change); no INR has been resulted since 9/10/2026 and the due date passed 7 days before the 9/24/2026 evaluation.

71-year-old man (DOB 1955-08-23) with coded atrial fibrillation (Condition 7010d0e5, ICD-9 427.31) restated in all cardiology notes through 7/28/2026. CHA2DS2-VASc = 3 (hypertension a85598ce, age 65-74 = 1, coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery 75b86cdb = vascular disease). Current medication is tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily only; no anticoagulant order is active on 2026-09-24. A remote coded 'hemorrhage complicating a procedure' (63df7d4c) is the only bleeding history and is not documented as an active contraindication, so guideline-recommended anticoagulation appears to be missing.

71-year-old woman (DOB 1955-09-07) with coded paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (Condition 66dd1300, ICD-10 I48.0); her single ECG (102298909, 3/14/2025) shows sinus rhythm with an isolated ectopic beat, consistent with paroxysmal AF. CHA2DS2-VASc = 5 (hypertension I10/4019, age 65-74 = 1, prior embolic cerebral infarction I6340/I639 with residual hemiplegia I69354 = 2, female). Current medications (last visit 7/10/2026) are carvedilol 6.25 mg twice daily, metoprolol tartrate 25 mg twice daily and famotidine; no anticoagulant order is active on 2026-09-24, so guideline-recommended (Class 1) oral anticoagulation is absent.

Apixaban 5 mg twice daily was re-ordered at the 8/20/2026 cardiology clinic visit (MedicationRequest dc397aff, valid through 2027) and is the current anticoagulant for atrial flutter. However the 8/12/2026 outside-records summary (DocumentReference 8fcbd349) documents an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer with haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL and 2 units transfused, and states that apixaban was held at discharge pending cardiology review. Anticoagulation has therefore been restarted after a major bleed without the documented review, and the patient is also on aspirin 81 mg plus clopidogrel 75 mg, compounding bleeding risk. Needs prescriber review.

Two different oral anticoagulants are simultaneously active on 2026-09-24: apixaban 5 mg twice daily (MedicationRequest 7206d5b5, authored 7/15/2026, valid to 1/2027) and rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (MedicationRequest b71a461f, authored 7/15/2026, valid to 1/2027). The 7/15/2026 clinic note (DocumentReference a80a007c) states the intent was to switch from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, but the rivaroxaban order was never stopped and the 7/15/2026 medication list still contains both. Duplicate anticoagulation markedly increases bleeding risk in this patient (AF/flutter, CKD stage 3, prior GI/rectal bleeding, thrombocytopenia) and must be reconciled.

The cardiology clinic note of 6/10/2026 (DocumentReference 96cdf346) states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded that same day - 107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36 - show atrial fibrillation: no organised P waves (P-wave amplitude 0.03-0.08 mV with beat-to-beat correlation 0.3-0.7) and markedly irregular RR intervals (coefficient of variation 0.16-0.19) at a mean ventricular rate of 132-136/min. The documented rhythm and rate are contradicted by the same-day tracings.

Escitalopram oxalate 10 mg daily is a QT watch-list drug and is the current order (MedicationRequest 8de890c6, 4/23/2026, valid to 1/2/2027); it has been continuous since it was started on 5/14/2024. The patient's most recent ECG (108018814, 10/8/2023) shows sinus rhythm at 68/min with QT 484 ms and Bazett QTc 516 ms, at or above the 500 ms threshold in the 1/15/2025 QT monitoring memo, so prescriber review is required. Most recent electrolytes (8/23/2025) are potassium 4.1 mEq/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL, both normal, so the prolongation is not explained by electrolyte depletion. Note the clinic note of 5/14/2024 described this tracing as 'QT acceptable'.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch list) is the current order (MedicationRequest 1014aca9, 7/29/2026, valid to 1/5/2027); amiodarone was started at the 11/10/2025 clinic visit. The most recent ECG (106885519, 11/24/2025 - obtained 14 days after amiodarone was started) shows sinus rhythm at 62/min with QT 528 ms and Bazett QTc 537 ms, well above the 500 ms threshold, and is a marked increase from the pre-amiodarone tracing of 6/7/2025 (QTc 423 ms). Most recent electrolytes (4/20/2026) potassium 4.4 mEq/L and magnesium 2.2 mg/dL are normal. The patient is also on warfarin, which amiodarone potentiates. Prescriber review required.
